text: Ọkọ́ rẹ̀ kúrú jù. Ọ̀nà ilẹ̀kùn rẹ̀ kéré jù. Ibùsùn rẹ̀ kúrú jù pẹ̀lú. Ọkùnrin yìí ga jù! Ó ṣe ọwọ ọkọ́ gígùn púpọ̀ kan. Ó ṣe ara ilẹ̀kùn gíga púpọ̀. Ó ṣe ibùsùn gígùn púpọ̀ kan. Ó kúrò ní ilé rẹ̀, ó sì gbé ní igbó ńlá kan. Ó gbé fún ọdún púpọ̀, ó sì láyọ̀.
selection_rationale: 9 sentences, 55 words, human protagonist (unnamed, matching the source), clear beginning (his tools don't fit)/middle (he remakes them)/end (he moves to the forest, content). Trimmed from the source's 13 sentences / 74 words by dropping the bicycle and chair/fork pages as secondary to the core arc, keeping the hoe/door/bed thread and the ending intact -- direct parallel structure to the Swahili sw-s-001 adaptation of the same source story.
source: Adapted, sentence-for-sentence from the actual published Yoruba translation, from 'Ọkùnrin gíga púpọ̀ kan' ('A Very Tall Man'), African Storybook, level 2, by Cornelius Gulere / Catherine Groenewald -- CC BY 3.0. Yoruba sentences quoted verbatim from the source pages except the final clause 'ó sì láyọ̀' (and he was happy), which is an addition not in the original text, added to give the trimmed version a clear positive ending -- mirrors the same addition made in the Swahili version of this story.
notes: The clause 'ó sì láyọ̀' at the end is an addition, not sourced -- flag for linguist check. Tone marking on the sourced sentences comes from a professional ASb translation so is higher-confidence than the two author-composed paragraphs above, but the added final clause is author-composed and needs the same level of scrutiny as those.

text: Adé fẹ́ràn ọgbà rẹ̀ gan-an. Ó gbin ẹfọ́ àti ẹ̀gẹ́ nínú ọgbà. Ní gbogbo ọjọ́, ó bu omi fún wọn. Ewéko náà ń dàgbà kíákíá. Ọjọ́ kan, ọ̀rẹ́ rẹ̀ Bísí wá sí ọgbà. Wọ́n jọ mú ẹfọ́ jáde papọ̀. Ìyá Adé se oúnjẹ dídùn pẹ̀lú ẹfọ́ náà. Gbogbo ẹbí jẹun papọ̀, wọ́n sì láyọ̀.
selection_rationale: 8 sentences, 54 words, human characters throughout (Adé, his friend Bísí, his mother, the family), clear beginning (Adé loves and tends his garden)/middle (his friend joins the harvest)/end (the family shares a meal, happy). NOT adapted from a real source -- see notes.
source: Author-created.
